A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CCDiff and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–C. Retained material can be matched reliably despite the added appendix content and renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original nuScenes closed-loop simulation comparisons, component ablations, causal-feature correlation analyses, and qualitative scenario-generation results in Section 5 and Appendix C.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and adds over-speed evaluation, gradient-conflict measurements, and inference-time scaling results in Appendix C.1.

M1.justification: v3 adds an evaluated over-speed guidance variant in Appendix C.1; v2 mentioned over-speed in its general reward formulation but evaluated collision/map guidance. This is a limited inference-objective extension; the architecture, training loss, causal ranking, and Algorithms 1–3 remain unchanged.

E1.justification: v3 adds actual over-speed scenario generation and evaluation, extending the collision-focused task coverage in v2. No additional dataset is identified, and the existing multi-agent, long-horizon, and seven qualitative scenario categories are retained.

E2.justification: SimNet, TrafficSim, STRIVE, BITS, and CTG retain their participation in the corresponding existing comparisons. The new over-speed and gradient-conflict experiments use the existing comparator CTG; no comparator is added to or removed from a retained experiment.

E3.justification: The added experiments introduce over-speed guidance with Scene Overspeed Rate, gradient-conflict diagnostics, and inference timing across agent counts. Existing data splits, 100-scene evaluation, history and rollout lengths, training budgets, and benchmark evaluation settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 adds direct analysis of the gradient-conflict mechanism through cosine similarity and the fraction of affected agents in Table 7, plus computational scaling analysis in Figure 6. Existing component ablations, causal-feature correlations, and qualitative case studies are preserved.

E5.justification: No repeated-run, seed, confidence-interval, or uncertainty-reporting changes are introduced. Existing correlation p-values are retained in v2 Table 8 and v3 Table 9. The new gradient-conflict averages and percentages are descriptive diagnostic results.

E6.justification: Existing results, including Tables 1–6, are unchanged. New Table 7 reports CTG/CCDiff SOR 0.68/0.73, SCR 0.35/0.33, ORR 4.23/0.89, CFD 15.81/9.65, the reported negative-gradient cosine statistic 1.85/1.29 in 10^-2 units, and conflict-agent percentages 9.12/4.79. Figure 6 adds generation-time scaling results.

T1.justification: Definitions 1–2, the constrained optimization formulation, score derivations, and guidance equations are unchanged. The added empirical diagnostics and DCG illustration introduce no new formal assumptions, propositions, proofs, or mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about causal composition improving realism and controllability in closed-loop traffic generation. The new appendix evidence does not redefine these main contributions.

C2.justification: v3 explicitly interprets the over-speed results as supporting extensibility to diverse safety-critical events and discusses measured conflict mitigation. Table 7's caption overstates uniform superiority, since higher-is-better SCR favors CTG. The conclusion's limitation concerning hyperparameter tuning and difficulty evaluating causal reasoning remains unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 newly discloses 15.4 million parameters and approximately 20 ms per frame per agent on an NVIDIA V100, alongside runtime scaling. These complement the retained training-resource and per-scenario timing disclosures. Existing hyperparameters and project/code links are unchanged; the over-speed guidance formula and threshold are not specified.

R1.justification: Section 2, Appendix A's comparison of related methods, and the same 53 cited works are retained. Reference-page pointers and pagination change, but the research positioning and cited-work membership do not.

P1.justification: v3 adds short explanatory paragraphs in Appendix C.1 and an acknowledgment, changes the author listing from Cyrus Huang to Xin Huang, and updates figure/table references. The existing prose and section organization are otherwise preserved.

P2.justification: v3 adds Table 7, a DCG-computation illustration in Figure 5, and an inference-scaling plot in Figure 6. Existing trajectory figures are retained and renumbered, with limited table-spacing and reference-layout changes.

improvement.justification: Compared with v2, v3 provides direct quantitative evidence for gradient-conflict mitigation, evaluates an additional control objective, and adds model-size and runtime information. These modestly strengthen empirical support and practical assessability. The gains are limited by sparse over-speed protocol details and Table 7's overstated caption: SCR favors CTG, 0.35 versus 0.33. These reporting weaknesses do not outweigh the added evidence and technical information.
